props.lead: Personalization pays in food tech, but less than vendors claim: 5–15% revenue lift in retail and only 1–2% in grocery[^a2c6][^a2c17], and the money is now made in retail media[^a2c11].

props.title: The lift is real, and small in grocery

props.text: McKinsey puts the revenue lift at 5–15% across retail, but only 1–2% of total sales for grocers[^a2c6][^a2c17].

props.caption: Grocery's 1–2% sits well below the broad-retail range, and the vendor figures sit far above it[^a2c17][^a2c4].

props.title: Vendor figures do not survive a filing

props.text: Starbucks' $2.1B and Domino's 63% appear only in marketing analyses, not in either company's reports[^a2c4][^a2c9].

props.question: How big is the revenue lift from personalization?

sides.label: Benchmarks
sides.summary: McKinsey puts the grocery lift at 1–2% of total sales[^a2c17].

props.title: The money is retail media, not data sales

props.text: Kroger's 84.51° says purchase-based targeting drove 4x the sales uplift with 50% fewer impressions[^a2c11].

props.caption: All three platforms report billion-dollar ad businesses, on different bases[^a2c12][^a2c13].

props.title: Diet data is policed by enforcement, not HIPAA

props.text: Most diet and delivery apps sit outside HIPAA, so the FTC acts as the de facto health-data regulator[^a3c5][^a3c6].
The FTC has gone as far as ordering WW and Kurbo to destroy the algorithms built on children's data[^a3c7].
